supporting_observations.claim: At 13:45:50 UTC, WS-ARUIZ-01 had a completed connection to the explicit web proxy on port 8080 with 51,000,536 bytes sent from the workstation and 9,009 bytes received. This is consistent with the alerted large outbound transfer, but identifies the proxy—not the ultimate destination.

The available record does not identify the process or user responsible for the large transfer, nor the requested URL or external recipient; the connection record provides only host, proxy endpoint, byte counts, and duration.

known_telemetry_limitations: The provided evidence has no matching proxy transaction record that identifies the destination, request method, user, user agent, or whether the proxy forwarded the transfer.
The available network record does not associate the connection with an endpoint process or a particular file.
The byte count is for traffic from WS-ARUIZ-01 to the proxy; the evidence does not establish how many bytes, if any, were forwarded by the proxy to an external service.
claims_not_established: Whether the transfer contained sensitive or organizational data.
Whether the transfer was authorized or intentional, or whether it was malicious.
The external destination or service involved, and whether that destination is approved.
Which user, process, or file initiated or supplied the transfer.
Whether the proxy successfully delivered the data beyond the organization.
additional_evidence_needed: Retrieve PROXY-PIN-01 transaction/access logs for the connection at approximately 13:45:50–13:46:14 UTC, including destination, request method, authenticated user, user agent, action, and upload/forwarded byte counts.
Correlate endpoint process-to-network telemetry on WS-ARUIZ-01 for the connection and obtain relevant file access, file creation, and DLP/audit records.
Identify the destination and data involved, then verify against approved services and, where possible, confirm the activity with the responsible user.
unrelated_findings: At 13:45:00 UTC, WS-ARUIZ-01 had an SMB connection to DC-PIN-01. This differs from the documented patching practice (admin workstation to FILE-PIN-01) and merits separate review; it is not evidence identifying or explaining the alerted proxy transfer. (T079-00168, T079-00170)

WS-ARUIZ-01 recorded repeated failed interactive logons for ana.ruiz at approximately 14:17–14:18 UTC. Their cause is not established here, and they are not linked by the available evidence to the alerted transfer. (T079-00415, T079-00422, T079-00428, T079-00429, T079-00431, T079-00432)
